title: Hardware-Software Co-design for Distributed Quantum Computing
problem: Distributed quantum computing requires remote entanglement generation, which is probabilistic and has long latency. Naive scheduling wastes opportunity to parallelize gate execution with entanglement generation.
method: Hardware-software co-design combining: (1) entanglement buffering to cache successfully-generated pairs, (2) asynchronous entanglement generation attempts in parallel with gate execution, (3) adaptive gate scheduling based on entanglement availability patterns.

title: BitPattern: Enabling Efficient Bit-Serial Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks through Bit-Pattern Pruning
problem: Bit-serial DNN accelerators struggle with unstructured bit sparsity, causing workload imbalance and inefficient memory access due to irregular non-zero bit distributions.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design: (1) algorithm level identifies optimal bit-pattern combinations via pruning, applies compression encoding for weight storage, merges similar patterns for workload balancing; (2) hardware implements bit-serial accelerator with dedicated pattern decoder and PE exploiting structured bit-pattern sparsity. Pattern-based approach vs bit-level irregularity.

title: Asymmetric Predictive Testing for Aging in SRAMs
problem: Current predictive testing methods for aging-induced SRAM failures use symmetric aggressive voltage conditions across read and write operations, resulting in significant over-testing that spuriously marks functional chips as defective.
method: The work identifies asymmetric aging in SRAM cells that preferentially store zeros and are more prone to read-1 failures. Proposes asymmetric testing: normal-voltage writes, aggressive-voltage read-0, and less-aggressive-voltage read-1. Introduces a statistical sampling and simulation method for fast convergence.

title: IDEA-GP: Instruction-Driven Architecture with Efficient Online Workload Allocation for Geometric Perception
problem: Robotic geometric perception tasks (SLAM, Structure from Motion) involve diverse and dynamically varying computational operators — including point cloud registration, pose graph optimization, bundle adjustment, and feature matching — whose workload fluctuates with environment and task, preventing static mapping to specialized accelerators and causing poor resource utilization.
method: IDEA-GP is an FPGA-based instruction-driven accelerator built around an array of general-purpose computational units (PEs) optimized for spatial-positioning representations such as rotation matrices, quaternions, and homogeneous coordinates. A compiler performs online workload analysis — profiling operator types and sizes at runtime — and emits PE-targeted instructions to dynamically schedule and pipeline optimization sub-problems (e.g., least-squares solve, graph relaxation). This instruction-driven dispatch allows the same PE array to handle the varied compute patterns of SLAM (incremental pose estimation, loop closure) and SfM (bundle adjustment, triangulation) without hardware reconfiguration. The system is deployed on a Xilinx ZCU102 evaluation board.

title: Dual-Issue Execution of Mixed Integer and Floating-Point Workloads on Energy-Efficient In-Order RISC-V Cores
problem: Single-issue in-order cores have limited instruction-level parallelism (IPC); dual-issue cores offer potential performance boost but with increased area and energy overhead. Mixed integer and floating-point workloads are common but underserved.
method: Develops COPIFT methodology and RISC-V ISA extensions enabling low-cost dual-issue execution of mixed integer and floating-point instruction sequences. The approach couples integer and floating-point functional units to reduce area overhead while maintaining timing, leveraging instruction-type diversity to achieve parallelism.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper MLP-Offload: Multi-Level, Multi-Path Offloading for LLM Pre-training to Break the GPU Memory Wall
method: Artifact evaluation of LLM pre-training offloading technique

title: What to Support When You're Compressing: The State of Practice Gaps and Opportunities for Scientific Data Compression
problem: Lossy compression widely adopted but impact on scientific outcomes poorly characterized; mismatch between app needs and compressor capabilities
method: Survey across 9 supercomputing application domains; characterizes workloads, application needs, and compressor capabilities

title: Optimal Respiratory Rate Estimation with mmWave Sensing Using PYNQ System-on-Chip Platform
problem: Non-invasive respiratory rate (RR) monitoring using mmWave requires embedded real-time signal processing. Existing approaches may not achieve high accuracy or require complex signal processing.
method: PYNQ platform-based implementation of range and respiration estimation. Signal processing pipeline: (1) Range FFT (RFFT), (2) Phase extraction and unwrapping, (3) FIR filtering, (4) Multiple RR estimation techniques with optimal weighted combination via quadratic cost function.

title: 2.2 IBM Telum II: Next Generation 5.5GHz Microprocessor with On-Die Data Processing Unit and Improved AI Accelerator
problem: Enterprise server workloads (z/OS) require high single-thread performance, large on-chip cache capacity, and specialized acceleration for AI and data processing. Previous generations face memory bandwidth bottlenecks for data-intensive workloads and limited AI compute integration.
method: Telum II is a 600mm² die in Samsung 5nm containing 43B transistors and 8 cores per chip (CP) operating at 5.5GHz. Key enhancements: (1) new on-die Data Processing Unit (DPU) for AI and data acceleration, (2) cache expansion: 10 L2 instances (36MB each, 40% larger than Telum) plus 360MB L3 (vs 256MB prior), (3) core shrink enabling cache growth while maintaining area, (4) microarch improvements: branch prediction, I-cache prefetch, additional rename registers, TLB optimization, (5) fully coherent multi-drawer architecture (up to 32 CP chips via drawer interconnects).

title: Power-Grid Structure Exploration with Unified Sequence-based Learning Framework
problem: Power-grid (PG) structure design at advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm) is critical for power integrity and performance, but design space exploration is complex; initial PG structures dominate optimization space.
method: Proposes a unified framework combining a novel sequence-based structure generator with a Transformer-based voltage-drop predictor. Learned embeddings from the predictor are used to identify promising PG structure candidates on the Pareto frontier during optimization. The sequence-based generator creates candidate PG topologies, while the Transformer predictor estimates static voltage-drop with high accuracy.

title: DREAM: Enabling Low-Overhead Rowhammer Mitigation via Directed Refresh Management
problem: JEDEC's Directed Refresh Management (DRFM) commands stall 8–32 DRAM banks simultaneously during Rowhammer mitigation, causing severe performance overheads (up to 49% slowdown) compared to the per-bank NRR assumed by prior work. Existing counter-based trackers that avoid these stalls require impractically large storage.
method: DREAM proposes two DRFM-aware variants. DREAM-R (randomized) delays issuing a DRFM after sampling an aggressor row so that other banks can also sample rows within the same window, amortizing the multi-bank stall across more mitigations per DRFM command. DREAM-C (counter-based) groups 32–256 randomly chosen rows across 32 banks into a 'gang' that shares a single counter, reducing tracker storage by 8x versus Graphene while avoiding CAM lookups and preserving DRFM compatibility.

title: TRACI: Network Acceleration of Input-Dynamic Communication for Large-Scale Deep Learning Recommendation Model
problem: Multi-GPU DLRM training is bottlenecked by embedding layer communication: the Aggregation collective (sparse, input-dependent gather/reduce across GPUs) cannot be accelerated by existing in-network compute solutions designed for All-Reduce because its data transfer patterns are dynamic and depend on input batch content, not topology.
method: TRACI introduces an in-network acceleration architecture with a novel network transaction design that augments messages with input reuse and output reuse identifications, allowing the network switch hardware to proactively identify and exploit message connections on-the-fly. New switch hardware dynamically discovers reuse relationships between embedding lookup requests arriving from different GPUs and performs in-network aggregation or deduplication rather than routing all data to a host.

title: 21.3 A Segmented-Interlacing Multi-Phase Hybrid Converter with Inherently Auto-Balanced ILs and Boosted IL Slew Rate During Load Transients
problem: Multi-phase buck/hybrid converters suffer from inductor current imbalance due to duty-cycle mismatches, requiring per-phase current sensing and closed-loop adjustment. Low inductor slew rate creates large output voltage undershoot during load transients.
method: Segmented-interlacing multi-phase hybrid converter with inherent auto-balancing via duty-cycle compensation and simultaneous energization of all inductors during load transients to boost slew rate, eliminating per-phase current sensing.

title: HeterRAG: Heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory Acceleration for Retrieval-augmented Generation
problem: RAG systems face two distinct memory bottlenecks: the retrieval stage suffers from random/irregular memory access patterns causing low bandwidth utilization, while the generation stage is bandwidth-limited by frequent GEMV operations over large LLM weights. Additionally, maintaining large-scale knowledge bases creates a capacity bottleneck that HBM-based PIM alone cannot satisfy.
method: HeterRAG combines HBM-based PIM and DIMM-based PIM in a heterogeneous system: DIMM-based PIM provides low-cost, high-capacity storage for large knowledge bases and accelerates the irregular memory accesses of the retrieval stage, while HBM-based PIM handles bandwidth-intensive GEMV operations in the generation stage. The architecture maps each RAG stage to the PIM type best suited to its access characteristics, coordinating data movement between the two PIM domains.

title: Unguided Machine Learning-Based Computation Offloading for Near-Memory Processing
problem: Data-intensive applications face memory wall bottlenecks in traditional processor-centric architectures. Supervised ML-based offloading requires extensive labeled datasets. Naive application-wide offloading to near-memory processing (NMP) cores underutilizes due to lower processing power.
method: Unsupervised clustering-based ML approach (UCO) that extracts application performance characteristics and creates two clusters (CPU-optimal vs. NMP-optimal regions) without requiring labeled training data. Targets only memory-intensive application regions for offloading.

title: Reproducible Performance Evaluation of OpenMP and SYCL Workloads under Noise Injection
problem: System noise (OS jitter, shared cache interference, NUMA effects) causes unpredictable performance variability in parallel computing. Existing evaluation methods cannot systematically characterize and mitigate noise effects on different parallel programming models.
method: Noise injection framework capturing real system traces and replaying them as controlled perturbations. Evaluation of OpenMP and SYCL workloads under both default and noise-injected conditions. Tested mitigation strategies: thread pinning, housekeeping core isolation, SMT toggling. Benchmarks: N-body, Babelstream; mini-app: MiniFE. Evaluation on two processor platforms.
